passage:
A school used to throw away broken chairs and desks quickly. Then a teacher started a repair club.
Students learned to tighten screws, sand wood, and replace small parts. They also recorded which items broke most often.
The school discovered that one model of chair failed in the same place again and again. Future purchases changed because of the club's report.
Repair became more than saving money. It became a source of information.
When something breaks, it can teach why it broke. A repair culture helps people see objects as systems, not trash waiting to happen.
